title: Investigate non-deterministic token duplication and softmax divergence under adaptive kernel routing
creator: Marco Chen
description: Observed non-deterministic token duplication and growing softmax score drift in production traces when adaptive kernel routing switches between fused-attn and fallback kernels mid-request. Problem appears intermittently on long-context prefill + streaming decode workloads. This ticket tracks a deep investigative effort to find root cause, mitigate customer-facing regressions, and implement a long-term fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a large prefill request (~2048 tokens) using model X with rotary embeddings enabled and mixed-precision path active
2) At ~prefill tail switch, send 1-2 concurrent decode requests that trigger adaptive kernel routing decision (force kernel A -> kernel B switch via synthetic load)
3) Observe token stream: duplication (repeated tokens) or insertion of previously-seen token ids during decode
4) Compare softmax outputs between run A (stable kernel path) and run B (kernel switch) to detect divergence beyond numerical epsilon
observed_behavior: Intermittent duplicated tokens emitted to clients during streaming decodes (1-3 duplicates per request)
Softmax logits diverging >1e-2 L2 distance after kernel switch (should be ~1e-6 under same seed/state)
KV-cache snapshot arithmetic mismatch at slot boundaries when kernel selection changes mid-request
Issue frequency increases under high scheduler load and opportunistic prefetching enabled
expected_behavior: Deterministic single token stream matching reference kernel run
Softmax outputs within numerical tolerance across kernel variants
KV cache continuity preserved across kernel routing events
initial_hypotheses: A. Memory alias / stale pointer: kernel swap leaves a small region of KV slots uninitialized or double-written leading to duplicated token generation
B. Quantization rounding mismatch: different kernels use slightly different fused-math sequences causing softmax instability to amplify during autoregressive steps
C. Scheduler preemption race: prefill/decoder handoff races can reorder updates to shared token index counters
D. Prefix/KV stitching bug: prefix cache merge does not reconcile overlapping kv-slot offsets when switching kernels
evidence_collected: Attached perf traces (perfetto) from failing run: https://redwood.internal/traces/rt-91802/trace-2026-03-04
Sample payloads and deterministic seed pairs uploaded: gs://redwood-debug/ENG-91802/samples.zip
Diff of logits between kernel-A-only vs kernel-A-then-B run: https://notebooks.redwood/internal/diffs/91802-softmax.html
Memory sanitizer output showing two small stale writes at KV slot boundary (see logs below)

investigation_notes: Reproduced locally with stress harness using deterministic scheduler; toggling opportunistic prefetch reduces frequency but does not eliminate duplication
Replaying failing trace with memory fencing and extra validation detects a second writer overlapping the end of prefix buffer
Floating point repro: switching kernels with identical inputs yields tiny per-layer differences that amplify in softmax during long autoregressive loops
Behavior correlated with batch composition: mixed prefill+decode in same worker more likely than isolated decode-only workers
actions_taken: 1) Rolled out temporary mitigation: disable opportunistic kernel switching for long-context (>1024) requests in runtime-1.22-edge (hotfix), throttled ramp to 50%
2) Added assert in KV write path to detect overlapping writes and log full stack traces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1247)
3) Built a unit test that runs A->B kernel switch loops for 10k iterations under ASAN to surface overlapping writes
4) Instrumented softmax paths to emit L2 diff metric for cross-kernel comparisons and surfaced to Console (dashboard link below)
links: Console dashboard for L2 softmax diffs: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/softmax-drift
next_steps: A) Root cause: confirm whether an incomplete fence/atomic causes overlapping KV writes when kernel buffer layouts differ; write small repro toggling fences
B) If race: convert KV write handoff to an atomic double-buffer swap ensuring readers only see fully-committed slots
C) If numerical amplification primary: harmonize softmax reduction numerics between kernels (reduce reorderings, use stable log-sum-exp path)
D) Run a canary of kernel-harmonization on dedicated capacity customers with long-context workloads (coordinate with SRE + CS)
E) Postmortem and public incident notes if customer-facing duplicates > 1% for affected tenants
commentary: 2026-03-02 Marco Chen: Initial report from SRE alerting on duplicated tokens observed in 3 customer calls. Assigned to Aisha to lead triage.
2026-03-03 Aisha Patel: Confirmed minimal reproducible case in CI stress harness. Hypothesis A (overlapping writes) looks promising after ASAN run.

2026-03-05 Priya Rao (ML Research): Measured softmax amplification; numerics alone explain divergence on very long autoregressive chains but not token duplication. Suggest focusing on memory/race for duplication and numerics for drift mitigation.
2026-03-07 Daniel Ortiz (SRE): Hotfix deployed to reduce opportunistic switching. Incident rate dropped by ~80% for affected tenants.
